title: The Social Cost of Intelligence: Emergence, Propagation, and Amplification of Stereotypical Bias in Multi-Agent Systems
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypical bias in religious contexts, as part of a broader study on bias in multi-agent systems.
findings: Multi-agent systems (MAS) tend to reproduce common social stereotypes, including those related to religion. Biases observed include associating atheists with being 'science-oriented', Christians as 'anti-science', Hindus with 'ritual/practice', and Muslims as 'violence-related'. These stereotypes emerge and can be amplified through agent interactions, particularly in competitive scenarios.
